known_issues: Kernel seals protect content and length, not origin, authentication, replay protection, encryption or release authority. Resolve packet/context expectations independently upstream.
Unix permissions are checked, not sealed. Plaintext access, swap handling and transport authorization remain responsibilities of the separately qualified outer boundary.

The producer context owns its borrowed descriptor. Callers must not close or reassign it; detected replacement is rejected without closing the replacement inode. Hostile concurrent manipulation of the same process descriptor table is outside this API contract.

Receiver reads use a close-on-exec duplicate and preserve borrowed offsets. Independently copied or explicitly inherited descriptors persist until their owners close them; context exit is not revocation.
Finite packet and chunk bounds do not qualify aggregate memory, CPU, deadline or descendant supervision. No service, process launcher, filesystem path or socket endpoint is introduced.
The original codec and snapshot job still own complete request and source/PDF validation. A sealed request can contain opaque invalid source that the original inspection must reject.
The default 32-page/8-MiB renderer is unchanged. Optional inspection uses the selected 64-page/16-MiB profiles. No scientific, accessibility or long-report release claim is added.
